evidence_quotes: Black Americans are ~13-14% of the US population but ~23-27% of those shot and killed, about 2 to 2.5x the per-capita rate for White Americans

Using arrests for violent crime or violent-crime rates as the denominator greatly shrinks or reverses the disparity. Using population as the denominator preserves it. There is no agreed correct denominator, and crime data themselves may reflect bias.
Per-population rates assume equal police exposure... There is no agreed correct denominator, and crime data themselves may reflect bias.

Fryer 2019, using Houston data, found no racial difference in shootings conditional on a stop, but large differences in non-lethal force... Ross, Winterhalder and McElreath 2021 and others argued that analysis suffers from collider bias... The literature remains divided precisely because causal identification is not possible from these counts alone.
